batch_node.name: Computing Core dimension v0.3.0
batch_node.description: Dimension nodes for the Computing Core plugin. v0.3.0: adds tap.computing.network_name and tap.computing.host, the two scope dimensions that address-bearing and host-scoped types key on (George 2026-11-12, aws-build Q47, Q49, Q50). v0.2.0: the identity category means accounts and groups defined on a host (os_user, os_group); the person type computing_core__user was retired (computing-core#27).

node.name: tap.computing
node.description: The computing dimension. All entity types and edges from the Computing Core plugin are tagged with tap.computing as their default dimension key, with category values: host (compute environments), runtime (programs and processes), storage (files and volumes), network (interfaces, addresses, ports, connections), protocol (application protocols above transport), and identity (accounts and groups defined on a host; a person is identity_core__human). This plugin provides vendor-neutral primitives that apply across cloud and on-prem environments.

node.name: tap.web
node.description: The web-native dimension. A future-boundary marker: web-native entity types (web_host, web_document) carry tap.web=native alongside their tap.computing stack-layer value. These were added to Computing Core under demo-time scope creep above the plugin's intended vendor-neutral-primitive line; the tap.web marker lets a future web_core plugin lift every web-native type and edge in one shot (MATCH on tap.web) without untangling them from the computing primitives.

node.name: tap.computing.network_name
node.description: The network an address belongs to. An address names one machine only within one address space: 10.0.0.5 in one VPC and 10.0.0.5 in another are different machines. The value is the name of a computing_core network node (a VPC id, a corporate network's name), and every public address uses the single value Internet. Open: values are network names, which keep arriving. It is the scope in the natural keys of address-bearing types (ip_address, port, and Tenable's dns_name and network_interface), so the same address seen by two sources in one network is one node.

node.name: tap.computing.host
node.description: The host a thing belongs to. The value is the host's own natural key as the spine stores it (realm|stable_id, for example ec2|i-0abc...), so a collector can compute it from source data before any row is resolved, and two grids agree on it. Open: one value per host. It is the scope in the natural keys of host-scoped types (loopback_address, os_user, os_group), where it never changes on a row. It is also stamped on ip_address, where it changes when the address moves to another host.
